To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The cosmic‐ray spectrum is expected to extend up to energies in the range 10 ^{20} –10 ^{21} eV; (ii) The flux is expected to fall as E ^{−2.7}, with a possible flattening at the highest energies; (iii) The composition is expected to be dominated by heavy elements; (iv) There is a possible indication of anisotropy at a level of a few percent;

the next generation of cosmic-ray experiments will have to be: (1) very sensitive to the highest energy cosmic‐ray fluxes; (2) capable of measuring the energy spectrum and the mass composition of the primary cosmic rays with a very high accuracy; and (3) able to determine the direction of the primary cosmic ray with an accuracy better than one degree.
